method_card.title: My Town and Local Area
method_card.content:
This lesson covers places in town, using il y a to describe what there is, on peut + infinitive to say what you can do, and comparisons using plus/moins/aussi... que.

FrenchEnglish
un magasina shop
un cinémaa cinema
un parca park
une piscinea swimming pool
une bibliothèquea library
un centre commerciala shopping centre
un muséea museum
une garea train station
une mairiea town hall
animé(e)lively
ennuyeux / ennuyeuseboring
tranquillequiet / peaceful
bruyant(e)noisy
pittoresquepicturesque
on peut + infinitifyou can / one can

Grammar focus — on peut + infinitive: On peut means 'you can' or 'one can'. It is always followed by an infinitive. Negative: on ne peut pas + infinitive. Example: On peut aller au cinéma le week-end. (You can go to the cinema at the weekend.) On ne peut pas nager ici. (You cannot swim here.)

Comparisons: Use plus... que (more... than), moins... que (less... than), aussi... que (as... as). Note: bon → meilleur(e) (not plus bon). Adjectives must agree with the noun they describe. Example: La ville est plus animée que la campagne.

Model paragraph: J'habite dans une petite ville dans le nord de l'Angleterre. Il y a un cinéma et beaucoup de magasins, mais il n'y a pas de piscine. On peut faire du shopping et aller au restaurant. Je préférerais habiter dans une grande ville parce que c'est plus animé. (I live in a small town in the north of England. There is a cinema and lots of shops, but there is no swimming pool. You can go shopping and go to a restaurant. I would prefer to live in a big city because it is more lively.)
steps: Learn the key places in town and their gender (un/une)
Use il y a and il n'y a pas de to describe what your town has or lacks
Use on peut + infinitive to say two things you can do in your town
Make comparisons with plus/moins/aussi... que and practise adjective agreement

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'On peut aller au cinéma le week-end et faire du shopping.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Break it down: On peut | aller au cinéma | le week-end | et | faire du shopping.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: On peut = You can / One can. Always followed by an infinitive. aller au cinéma = go to the cinema.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: le week-end = at the weekend. faire du shopping = go shopping. Note: French uses du before shopping because it is a masculine noun.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: You can go to the cinema at the weekend and go shopping.

worked_examples.question: How do you make comparisons in French?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Use plus + adjective + que for 'more... than': La ville est plus animée que la campagne.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Use moins + adjective + que for 'less... than': La campagne est moins bruyante que la ville.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: Exception: bon → meilleur(e) (not plus bon). The adjective must agree with the first noun. La campagne est plus tranquille (feminine → tranquille).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: plus/moins/aussi + adjective + que. Exception: bon → meilleur(e). The adjective agrees with the first noun in the comparison.

bronze.question: Match the French places in town to the English meaning
Match the French adjectives to the English meaning
Complete the sentence with the correct word
sentence_parts: aller au cinéma le week-end, mais on ne
pas nager parce qu'il n'y a pas de piscine.

gaps.correct_explain: peut is the on form of pouvoir. On peut = you can / one can.
On ne peut pas = you cannot. The ne...pas wraps around peut.

bronze.question: Complete the comparison
sentence_parts: la campagne, mais la campagne est

wrong.moins: moins means 'less'. The city is more lively than the countryside.

gaps.correct_explain: que means 'than' in comparisons: plus animée que la campagne.

wrong.de: de is not used in comparisons. Use que for 'than'.

gaps.correct_explain: moins + adjective = less... The countryside is less polluted.

wrong.plus: plus polluée = more polluted — but the countryside is less polluted.

bronze.question: What does 'Il y a beaucoup de magasins mais il n'y a pas de piscine' mean?
options: There are lots of shops but there is no swimming pool
There are no shops but there is a swimming pool
There are lots of museums and a swimming pool
There were lots of shops and a swimming pool

bronze.question: Which sentence means 'The city is more lively than the countryside'?
options: La ville est plus animée que la campagne.
La ville est moins animée que la campagne.
La ville est aussi animée que la campagne.
La ville est meilleure que la campagne.

bronze.source_text: On peut faire du shopping et manger au restaurant, mais la ville est assez bruyante.
model_answers: You can go shopping and eat at the restaurant, but the town is quite noisy.
You can go shopping and eat at a restaurant, but the city is quite noisy.
hints: faire du shopping = to go shopping

bronze.audio_text: Il y a un parc et un cinéma en ville.
bronze.correct_text: Il y a un parc et un cinéma en ville.
bronze.translation: There is a park and a cinema in town.

silver.question: Complete the sentence by typing the correct word

gaps.correct_explain: peut is the on form of pouvoir. On peut + infinitive = you can.
municipale is feminine to agree with la piscine (feminine noun).

wrong.municipal: municipal is the masculine form. La piscine is feminine, so use municipale.

silver.english: You can swim at the municipal swimming pool.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: La campagne est plus bon que la ville pour la santé.
silver.explanation: Bon has an irregular comparative: meilleur(e) (better), not plus bon. Since la campagne is feminine, use meilleure.
silver.translation: The countryside is better than the city for health.

silver.question: Build the sentence in French
silver.english: You can visit museums in the town centre.

distractor_labels.peux: wrong form — on uses peut, not peux (which is je/tu)

silver.source_text: There is a cinema and a park. You can walk in the park on Saturdays.
model_answers: Il y a un cinéma et un parc. On peut se promener dans le parc le samedi.
Il y a un cinéma et un parc. On peut marcher dans le parc le samedi.

gold.source_text: I live in a small town in the north of England. There is a cinema and lots of shops, but there is no swimming pool. The town is quite boring in the evening. I would prefer to live in a big city because it is more lively.
model_answers: J'habite dans une petite ville dans le nord de l'Angleterre. Il y a un cinéma et beaucoup de magasins, mais il n'y a pas de piscine. La ville est assez ennuyeuse le soir. Je préférerais habiter dans une grande ville parce que c'est plus animé.

gold.question: Build the sentence in French
gold.english: The countryside is less noisy than the city.

distractor_labels.Le: wrong gender — campagne is feminine, needs La not Le
distractor_labels.de: wrong word — comparisons use que (than), not de
distractor_labels.bruyant: wrong gender — la campagne is feminine, needs bruyante not bruyant

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are on an exchange trip in France. A French student asks you about your hometown. You are speaking to your host in their home.

bullets.prompt: Describe your town — say where it is and what there is.
bullets.model_answer: J'habite dans une petite ville dans le nord de l'Angleterre. Il y a un cinéma, un parc et beaucoup de magasins.
bullets.note: habiter + dans + location. Il y a + places in town

bullets.prompt: Say two things you can do in your town.
bullets.model_answer: On peut faire du shopping au centre commercial et on peut aller au restaurant.

bullets.prompt: Compare your town with the countryside.
bullets.model_answer: La ville est plus animée que la campagne, mais la campagne est moins polluée.
bullets.note: plus... que / moins... que with adjective agreement

bullets.prompt: Say where you would prefer to live and why.
bullets.model_answer: Je préférerais habiter dans une grande ville parce que c'est plus animé et il y a plus de choses à faire.

gold.question: Listen and type what you hear
gold.audio_text: J'habite dans une petite ville. Il y a un cinéma et beaucoup de magasins. Je préférerais habiter dans une grande ville parce que c'est plus animé.
gold.correct_text: J'habite dans une petite ville. Il y a un cinéma et beaucoup de magasins. Je préférerais habiter dans une grande ville parce que c'est plus animé.
gold.translation: I live in a small town. There is a cinema and lots of shops. I would prefer to live in a big city because it is more lively.

gold.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
gold.sentence: Les restaurants en ville sont plus bons que ceux à la campagne.
gold.explanation: Bon has an irregular comparative: meilleur(e)(s), not plus bon(s). Since les restaurants is masculine plural, use meilleurs.
gold.translation: The restaurants in town are better than those in the countryside.
